headline: Cyclopharm CEO acknowledges share price disconnect from operational momentum, attributing it to thin trading and pointing to continued US delivery as the key re-rating catalyst.
reasoning: Despite strong operational metrics — record revenue, doubling of US installations, peak cash burn passed, and 90%+ consumable margins — the share price has not responded in kind. The CEO attributes this partly to the stock being thinly traded. He believes the market is not pricing in the full opportunity and that continued execution in the US will be the turning point. Institutional shareholders are described as supportive, and the company is focused on delivering on its US strategy as the primary value driver.
quote: Every indicator that we've just talked about, it's kind of going the other way from what you see on the share price, I think, you know, we're thinly traded share. And you know, my focus is is just delivering on the US. And I suppose that's going to be the turning point for us.
episode_title: The Aussie small cap betting big on the US

headline: Cyclopharm CEO highlights record first-half 2026 revenue driven by accelerating US installations of Technegas, with margins above 90% on consumables and a long runway to 2,000 target sites.
reasoning: Cyclopharm reported record first-half 2026 revenue of $17.5 million, up 14%, with US revenue up 74% year-on-year. Installations of its radioactive diagnostic agent Technegas in the US doubled from 35 to 70 at the half and reached 83 by the time of reporting, against a target market of approximately 2,000 sites out of more than 5,100 doing these procedures. Consumable gross margins exceed 90% and are expected to expand further as the US business scales. Newly released US nuclear medicine clinical practice guidelines are seen as a game-changer and a key commercial tool, given there is no comparable product in the marketplace. The company operates in 67 countries and holds approximately 85% market share in established markets, with a similar outcome expected in the US over time. Cash burn has already peaked, with the business now moving toward sustained margin expansion.
quote: That's certainly the foundation but across the board Andrew all of the things that you know, we've been working on, um, have delivered the growth. You're right. 17.5 up, uh, up 14% US up 74%... at the half last year, we were at 35 installations at the, at the half, uh, this year were at 70. And even at the time of the report, we were at 83. So we've seen that acceleration. And one of the things that that not even baked into that number yet is the guidelines. I think last time I was here talking about the the nuclear medicine guidelines that were just released in the US, we believe that is a game changer for us.
episode_title: The Aussie small cap betting big on the US

headline: Cyclopharm CEO flags US market delivery as key re-rating catalyst despite depressed share price
reasoning: James McBrayer acknowledges that Cyclopharm's share price does not reflect the company's positive operating indicators, attributing this partly to thin trading. He says the focus is squarely on executing in the US market, which he sees as the turning point for the company's valuation. He notes the company is already seeing strong early success in the US and that a loyal institutional shareholder base remains supportive, expecting continued delivery on growth expectations.
quote: What is the market not seeing? Well, you know, every indicator that we've just talked about, it's kind of going the other way from what you see on the share price, I think, you know, we're thinly traded share. And you know, my focus is is just delivering on the US. And I suppose that's going to be the turning point for us... we are seeing some great success in the market right now.
episode_title: The Aussie small cap betting big on the US

headline: Cyclopharm CEO highlights accelerating US growth as first 11-site hospital deal signals enterprise-scale adoption of Technegas lung imaging agent
reasoning: Cyclopharm has signed its first double-digit, all-at-once installation deal with University Hospitals across 11 US sites, marking a step-change from the typical one-or-two-site test-and-grow model seen at Massachusetts General, Stanford, and Emory. The US business model is lease-based rather than capital-sale, reducing customer capex barriers and accelerating rollout while generating high-margin consumable annuity revenues. US revenues grew 73% in the latest half, from ~$1.1m to over $2m, and revenue-generating installations rose from 50 at the AGM to 70 by end of July. Upcoming US clinical guidelines are expected to name Technegas as the agent of choice, reinforcing its already globally recognised clinical positioning across 67 countries. McBrayer also flagged AI as a future growth vector, given the rich functional lung data the product generates, with clinical trials underway with multiple partners.
quote: University Hospitals is our first double digit all at once in in the installation deal. Usually what we see is one of the sites will will come on board at 1 or 2 locations and then grow from there. We've seen that at Massachusetts General Stanford. Uh, Emory, this is our first example of, uh, instead of test driving it, they've bought a whole fleet for the family... our consumables are certainly in the US are a very high margin business. Every time we do an installation that that revenue starts dropping to the bottom line... the US went from about, you know, 1.1 million to just over two, $2 million. So we've had 73% increase in in the US.
episode_title: Cyclopharm's US growth story gathers pace
